objects.what: Tokenizer for SMS/push templates. It does NOT build the final text. It only returns the list of placeholder tokens (words that contain '@') so the caller can resolve them. Signature :23: @Mensaje varchar(300), @Cuenta varchar(10), @CuentaF varchar(10), @Articulo varchar(10). Returns @Estructura(ID identity, Llave varchar(150), Valor varchar(150), Cuenta, CuentaF, Articulo all varchar(10)) (:24-32). Steps: (1) the first 150 chars are copied to @MensajeAux varchar(150) (:45) and only that copy is checked for '@' (:49). (2) If an '@' is found, every space becomes ',' (:57-61). The string is then cut on ',' in a WHILE/CHARINDEX/SUBSTRING loop (:63-75), and the remainder after the last delimiter is added (:77-82). A message with no delimiter is inserted whole (:83-87). Only tokens containing '@' are returned, with Valor='' and the passed Cuenta/CuentaF/Articulo (:89-97). (3) If there is no '@' in the first 150 chars, a single row is returned with Llave = the whole @Mensaje, up to 300 chars (:100-111). The @LlaveValor table variable (:37-43) is declared and never used. Only spaces and existing commas split tokens. '.', ':', ';', ')', ']', tab, CR and LF do not, so they stay attached to the token. CALLER USE (SpAAEA00030_ArmadoSMS.sql): CROSS APPLY dbo.FnAAea00030_SplitString(Mensaje, Cliente, ClienteF, ISNULL(Articulo,'')) at :559 inserts into #Estructura (:536-558). Each Llave is exact-joined to TcAAea00030_VariablesArmadoSMS.Variable (:608). The matching Query gets @Cuenta/@ClienteF/@Articulo replaced (:591) and runs as dynamic SQL (:642-653). REPLACE(Mensaje, Llave, Valor) is applied to the template once per token (:671-679). The output is CONCAT(Mensaje, ISNULL(ClaveSms,'')) (:688). The OTP Clave is appended after expansion and never passes through the split. For the opening NIP SMS (IdMensaje 14, queued by SpCREDISolicitudWebPrimerGuardado SaveNip :189-266 with Cliente 'CW00001', ClienteF NULL, Clave=@ClaveMensaje :222-249), the function receives Cuenta='CW00001' and Articulo=CAST(PG.IdSolicitudWebDatosPrimerGuardado AS VARCHAR) (ArmadoSMS :302-307). An INT is at most 10 chars, so neither parameter is truncated. CAN IT DROP OR TRUNCATE? (a) It never silently drops a single message. If '@' is in the first 150 chars, some token has '@'. A NULL template goes to the ELSE branch and returns a NULL row. So the function always returns at least one row and the CROSS APPLY never removes a message. (b) It can abort the whole batch. A template longer than 150 chars with no '@' in its first 150 chars goes to the ELSE branch, and inserting it into Llave varchar(150) (:27,103-109) raises 'String or binary data would be truncated' (Msg 8152/2628). This also happens when the first placeholder sits after char 150. ArmadoSMS needs ANSI_WARNINGS ON because it reads the linked server ERPMAVI (:9-10,266,441), so the error is raised rather than silently truncating. The error fails the INSERT at :536, so the SP returns nothing: every SMS for that @IdUsuarioSMS plus all push rows (push is not filtered by user, :470-473), the NIP SMS included. The rows keep EstatusEnvio=1 and the problem repeats on every run. The 2021 header 'se amplía el tamaño de la llave … sin variable' (:20, ArmadoSMS :114-115) shows this already happened once. A template longer than 300 chars fails the same way at #Estructura.Mensaje VARCHAR(300) (ArmadoSMS :492). An expansion that pushes the text past 300 fails at #LlaveValor.Mensaje VARCHAR(300) (:515,672-678). (c) It can send a NIP SMS with no NIP. A placeholder glued to punctuation or a newline ('@Nip.', 'NIP:@Nip', '@Nip\n') becomes Llave '@Nip.', which does not match VariablesArmadoSMS. The Query is then NULL, nothing runs (:653) and the text is not replaced (:671). The SMS goes out with the literal placeholder and no NIP. (d) Parameter truncation is silent. Values longer than varchar(10) passed as Cuenta/CuentaF/Articulo are cut to 10 with no error, for example Articulo = EM.Parametro for IdMensaje 34 (ArmadoSMS :327-328). The variable query then runs with the wrong key. This does not affect IdMensaje 14. (e) Placeholder order: REPLACE order follows ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY ID) (:562-563), which is arbitrary. If one variable name is a prefix of another (for example @Nombre and @NombreD), the longer one can be corrupted. Whether template 14 hits (b), (c) or (e) depends on DB data I have not seen. I did not run SQL. The user must check it (queries in evidence).

defects: Batch-wide abort: a template longer than 150 chars with no '@' in its first 150 chars (including one whose first placeholder is after char 150) goes to the ELSE branch. Inserting it into Llave varchar(150) (:27,:103-109) raises Msg 8152/2628 under ANSI_WARNINGS ON, which ArmadoSMS needs for its ERPMAVI linked-server reads (:9-10). INSERT #Estructura (ArmadoSMS :536-559) fails and the SP returns no rows. Every queued SMS for that @IdUsuarioSMS and all push rows are blocked, the NIP SMS included, and the rows stay EstatusEnvio=1 and fail again on every run.

Placeholder detection only looks at the first 150 chars (@MensajeAux varchar(150), :45,:49) while the parameter takes 300 (:23). A placeholder after char 150 in an otherwise variable-free prefix is never expanded. With ANSI_WARNINGS OFF it would go out as the literal '@Var'. With ON it causes the abort above.

Only space and comma split tokens (:57-61). A placeholder followed by '.', ':', ';', ')', ']', tab or CR/LF becomes a Llave such as '@Nip.' that does not exact-match TcAAea00030_VariablesArmadoSMS.Variable (ArmadoSMS :608). It is not replaced (:671) and the SMS goes out with no value, which for template 14 would mean a NIP SMS without the NIP. Depends on the template text (DB data).

Silent truncation of @Cuenta/@CuentaF/@Articulo to varchar(10) at the parameter boundary (:23). Example: IdMensaje 34 passes EM.Parametro as Articulo (ArmadoSMS :327-328), and the variable query then runs with a cut key. IdMensaje 14 is not affected (Cliente 'CW00001', Articulo = INT id of at most 10 chars).

Caller-side limits on the same path: #Estructura.Mensaje and #LlaveValor.Mensaje are VARCHAR(300) (ArmadoSMS :492,:515). A template over 300 chars, or one that grows past 300 after REPLACE (:672-678), aborts the whole batch the same way.

REPLACE order is arbitrary (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY ID), ArmadoSMS :562-563). A variable whose name is a prefix of another (for example @Nombre and @NombreD) can corrupt the longer one. A repeated placeholder produces duplicate rows and runs the variable query again.
Any '@' word that is not a variable (an e-mail address or social handle in the template) is returned as a token. It is harmless (no Variable match) but costs a loop iteration with EXEC(NULL).
Dead code: the @LlaveValor table variable (:37-43) and the IF @Delimitador = ' ' test, which is always true (:57). ArmadoSMS also declares @Mensaje VARCHAR(150) (:483) and never uses it.

objects.what:
Marks one mobile number of a client as validated in CteTel, stamps who validated it, and un-validates every other number of that client. Params @Cliente VARCHAR(10), @Telefono VARCHAR(10), @AppOrigen VARCHAR(50) (:14-16). (1) When LEN(@Telefono)=10, it splits lada/number: if the first 2 digits are a 2-digit lada in TablaStD '1138ValAutLadaTel', then lada=2 digits and number=last 8; otherwise lada=3 digits and number=last 7 (:24-40). (2) It checks for an existing CteTel row with Cliente=@Cliente, CONCAT(Lada,Telefono)=@Telefono and Tipo='Movil' (:42-54). (3a) If one exists, it runs UPDATE CteTel SET ValidacionTel=1, AppOrigen=@AppOrigen, Fecha=GETDATE() and sets @Resultado=@@ROWCOUNT (:56-70). (3b) If not, it runs INSERT CteTel(Cliente, Lada, Telefono, ValidacionTel=1, Tipo='Movil', AppOrigen=@AppOrigen, Fecha, FechaCaptura) and sets @Resultado=SCOPE_IDENTITY(), which is the new id_tel, not a row count (:72-96). (4) If @Resultado>0, it runs UPDATE CteTel SET ValidacionTel=0 for every other row of the client with CONCAT(Lada,Telefono)<>@Telefono, with no Tipo filter, so it also hits non-Movil rows.
